title: Structured GPU bundle provenance and staged rollback policy
creator: Ethan Liu
description: Goal: Create a deterministic, auditable artifact-to-driver provenance model and an automated staged rollback policy for GPU-accelerated runtime bundles (container image + SBOM + pinned CUDA/driver stacks). This ticket will deliver a bundle manifest format, validation pipeline, rollout gate definitions, and an operational rollback playbook so customers on LTS channels can upgrade with low risk.
work_items: Define bundle manifest schema capturing: image digest, SBOM checksum, signed driver artifact ID, OS kernel compatibility window, required kernel modules, kernel ABI fingerprint, and KMS key ID for signing.
Implement CI validator that emits a deterministic provenance document and fails PRs when SKU/driver mismatches are detected.
Add a rollout gate stage to the existing release pipeline: static checks -> canary cohort (2%) -> regional ramp -> global. Each stage runs smoke, perf, and kernel-compat tests.
Build a rollback plan generator that computes a minimal rollback set and quarantines affected nodes via autoscaler hooks and image pinning enforcement.
Integrate signed manifests into artifact registry UI and Console rollouts UI with visibility for token-level cost/latency impacts.
Publish runbook for on-call with playbook steps, required dashboards, and postmortem checklist.
Add unit and integration tests for SBOM delta detection, driver ABI compatibility checks, and signature verification using customer KMS mock.
acceptance_criteria: Manifest schema documented in Confluence and accepted by release engineering and platform security.
CI validator deployed in runtime repo and blocking merges for mismatched bundles (proof: PR #1234 shows failure on incompatible driver).
Rollout gate automation executes staged canary deployment and automatically halts on regression signals (p95 latency increase > 30% or error-rate > 0.5%).
Rollback plan generator produces a human-readable plan and a machine-consumable manifest that the autoscaler and console can execute within 5 minutes of decision.
Signed provenance artifacts surfaced in Console UI with direct links to SBOM and image registry entries.
Runbook validated in a simulated upgrade and a war room drill (notes attached).
comments: 2026-02-16 - Ethan Liu: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed to use a single canonical manifest that can be signed with KMS and stored in the artifact registry. Priya to prototype schema.
2026-02-20 - Priya Nair: Prototype manifest v0 submitted as PR #1250. Needs fields for kernel ABI fingerprint and module whitelist. Security requested explicit KMS key ID and signature timestamp.
2026-02-24 - Miguel Torres (Security): Reviewed schema; requested immutable SBOM checksums and signature verification in CI. Also asked for an opt-in customer-facing audit URL pattern.

2026-03-01 - Priya Nair: Implemented CI validator skeleton and smoke test harness for canary cohorts. Initial canary run in staging passed smoke but perf regression observed on p95 for 40-token tailcases; investigating batching/kernel scheduler interaction.

2026-03-03 - Eng Infra review: Decided to keep driver-pin list separate from image metadata to allow micro-rollbacks of driver bundles without forcing image rebuilds. Trade-off: slightly more complexity in rollout automation but faster recovery.

2026-03-05 - Priya Nair: Updated acceptance criteria to include automated halt thresholds and rollback plan time budget. Next: wiring the validator into the protected branch and setting up a demo for Platform PM.
